what_happened: A docs job to clarify the firstmate study page (jargon, diagram, tags, card titles) was rejected at final verification. One of 8 acceptance criteria was unmet: the glossary and cards must use two distinct terms for firstmate's deciding part and for the workers, and the page must state which one 'decided by' refers to. The verifier raised one major finding: the cards still use 'agent' for both the deciding part and the workers. It cited six places in studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json (lines 18, 44, 80, 83, 90, 104) and two in xtask/src/site.rs (lines 377, 392). No failed checks are listed. The glossary was probably fixed, but the card text and the site generator were not.
cause: A terminology change is spread across several files: the data model and the Rust site generator. Nothing in the job's process searches the whole repo for the old term before the job finishes. The work was judged complete from the glossary edit alone. The unmet criterion was found only by the final verifier, after all the work was done. Athena has no step that turns a 'no longer used for both' criterion into a mechanical sweep that the builder runs and passes before handing over.
prevention: Add a pre-verification check for criteria of the form 'term X is no longer used for Y'. The check greps all job-owned files (model.json, site.rs, glossary and card text) for the retired term. It lists every remaining occurrence, and the job cannot move to final verification until each one is either replaced or on an explicit allowlist with a reason. The builder runs the check and attaches its output to the job, so the gap is caught during the work instead of at the final verdict.
proposed_request: On the firstmate study page, make the wording consistent so a newcomer never sees one word for two things. Use one term for firstmate's deciding part and a different term for the workers. Apply them everywhere the page shows them: the glossary, every card in studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json, and the text generated by xtask/src/site.rs. State on the page which of the two terms 'decided by' refers to. Before finishing, search all those files for the word 'agent' and confirm every remaining use is unambiguous, or has been replaced. Include the search output in the job. Done when no card or generated text uses one word for both the deciding part and the workers, and the page says what 'decided by' means.
